sections.markdown:
## A — Exam authority for the driving under the influence and license suspensions and revocations section (Nevada Basic Class C driver license knowledge test)
Issuer: the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles publishes the Nevada Driver's Handbook and says the knowledge test for a Nevada license draws on what the handbook contains [A01].
Source document: the Nevada Driver's Handbook whose front cover carries the form and edition line DMV 700 March 2024 [A02].
Edition freshness: this edition was already about two and a half years old when it was staged, so whether it is still the current one stays open until the DMV confirms it (verify NV-DUIS-A-FRESH).
Knowledge test format: it checks your grasp of highway signs and markings, traffic laws and safe driving practices, on automated testing equipment or on paper; an oral exam can be requested, and Basic Class C testing is also offered in Spanish [A03].
Vision: every applicant has vision checked against minimum standards, and needing glasses or contact lenses to drive puts a restriction on the license [A03].
Question count, passing standard and time limit: the handbook states none of them, so all three stay unknown and are never shown to learners (verify NV-DUIS-A-COUNT, NV-DUIS-A-PASS, NV-DUIS-A-TIME).
This section feeds the knowledge test: the knowledge test checks traffic laws, and this section carries Nevada's DUI law in detail: the alcohol and marijuana limits, implied consent and refusal, illegal per se levels for adults, drivers under twenty-one and commercial drivers, the administrative and criminal penalty ladder, ignition interlock, young-driver rules, the open container law, impaired-driver clues, and the grounds for license suspension and revocation.
Practice quizzes follow the product mastery policy from the learning loop, which is not an official exam threshold.
